summary: A free botanical-style public park in the Chatuchak green-space complex, with more than 2,000 plant species, lotus gardens, themed plant collections, lawns and ponds. It suits a quiet stroll or a nature break alongside Chatuchak Park and Wachirabenchathat Park.
whyGo: Explore themed gardens and a large lotus lawn in a leafy setting near Chatuchak market and museums.
Walk or run the garden paths, rest beside the ponds, and look for plant labels and collections.
Pair the visit with neighbouring parks for a longer green-space outing.
bestFor: Garden and plant enthusiasts, walkers, runners, and families wanting an outdoor break.
Visitors already going to Chatuchak or the nearby Children’s Discovery Museum.
A low-cost visit reachable by BTS or MRT.
skipIf: You need a late-evening park visit; the listed closing time is 19:00.
You want guaranteed seasonal flowers in December or extensive indoor attractions.
You plan to cycle, bring a pet, fly a drone, or smoke; the BMA lists these as prohibited.
duration: Allow around 1–2 hours for a relaxed garden walk; this is a planning estimate, and combining the adjoining parks takes longer.
cost: General admission is free. The BMA currently lists toilets at 5 baht and parking as free for the first 15 minutes, then 20 baht for the first hour; confirm current charges on arrival.
hours: The BMA lists daily hours of 05:00–19:00. Hours can change for maintenance, events or holidays; check the official listing before a December visit.
bestTime: Visit early morning or late afternoon for a more comfortable walk. BMA highlights yellow royal trumpet tree and purple-pink indigo blooms, while an official district description says the trees flower around February–May; do not plan on those peak blooms in December.
gettingThere: The BMA lists BTS Mo Chit and MRT Chatuchak Park stations, plus buses 77, 122, 136 and 145 and variants. The park entrance is on Kamphaeng Phet 2 Road; check a live map for the best station exit and current bus service.
booking: No booking is indicated for ordinary park entry. Contact the park for group botanical tours, field trips, or venue requests; the official park site lists queenpark72@gmail.com for inquiries.
accessibility: The park includes a garden designed for visitors with visual impairments, according to the BMA listing. The reviewed information does not detail step-free access, accessible toilets, path surfaces, or mobility-aid services across the wider grounds; contact the park at 02-272-4374 about specific needs.
practicalTips: Wear walking shoes and bring water and sun protection; much of the visit is outdoors.
Leave bicycles and pets outside the park and observe posted rules; the BMA also prohibits smoking, alcohol and drones.
The official listing mentions the large lotus lawn, Thai plant building and themed gardens; check which buildings are open if those are a priority.
Use the neighboring parks to extend the outing, but allow time to return before this park’s listed 19:00 closing.
decemberNotes: December is a pleasant season for an outdoor walk compared with Bangkok’s hotter months, though it can still be warm and air quality varies. The prominent tree blooms described by the BMA and district source are associated with roughly February–May, so December is not a reliable peak-flower period. No special December 2026 event schedule or holiday-hours notice was confirmed.
uncertainties: Hours, fees and park rules may change before December 2026; reconfirm with the BMA listing or park office.
Detailed accessibility information for paths, toilets and entrances is not published in the reviewed sources.
Opening hours of individual garden buildings and the Children’s Discovery Museum are separate and were not confirmed here.
No December 2026 events or temporary closures were confirmed.
